item_name: High-Risk Drug Classes: Use and Indication — Antianxiety

lookback_source.quote: N0415B1. Antianxiety: Check if an anxiolytic medication was taken by the resident at any time during the 7-day look-back period (or since admission/entry or reentry if less than 7 days).

lookback_notes: 7-day look-back period, or since admission/entry or reentry if the stay is less than 7 days. The item table on p. N-4 states the window as "during the last 7 days or since admission/entry or reentry if less than 7 days." The manual uses "7-day look-back period" (N0415B1, p. N-7) and "7-day observation period"/"observation period" (Coding Instructions, p. N-6; N0415B2, p. N-7) interchangeably for the same 7-day window.

coding_levels.label: Antianxiety — Is taking
coding_levels.definition: Check if an anxiolytic medication was taken by the resident at any time during the 7-day look-back period (or since admission/entry or reentry if less than 7 days).

source.quote: N0415B1. Antianxiety: Check if an anxiolytic medication was taken by the resident at any time during the 7-day look-back period (or since admission/entry or reentry if less than 7 days).

coding_levels.label: Antianxiety — Indication noted
coding_levels.definition: Check if there is an indication noted for all anxiolytic medications taken by the resident any time during the observation period (or since admission/entry or reentry if less than 7 days).

source.quote: N0415B2. Antianxiety: Check if there is an indication noted for all anxiolytic medications taken by the resident any time during the observation period (or since admission/entry or reentry if less than 7 days).

coding_levels.label: Not taking / no indication noted
coding_levels.definition: Item column left unchecked; Column 2 is only considered if Column 1 is checked. Per the item table, Column 2 is checked only if Column 1 is checked and an indication is noted for all medications in the drug class.

source.quote: If Column 1 is checked, check if there is an indication noted for all medications in the drug class

federal_coding_rules.rule: Column 1 (Is taking): check if the resident is taking any medications by pharmacological classification, not how it is used, during the last 7 days or since admission/entry or reentry if less than 7 days.

source.quote: Check if the resident is taking any medications by pharmacological classification, not how it is used, during the last 7 days or since admission/entry or reentry if less than 7 days

federal_coding_rules.rule: Column 2 (Indication noted): if Column 1 is checked, check if there is an indication noted for all medications in the drug class.

source.quote: If Column 1 is checked, check if there is an indication noted for all medications in the drug class

federal_coding_rules.rule: Code all high-risk drug class medications according to their pharmacological classification, not how they are being used.

source.quote: Code all high-risk drug class medications according to their pharmacological classification, not how they are being used.

federal_coding_rules.rule: Column 1: check if the resident is taking any medications by pharmacological classification during the 7-day observation period (or since admission/entry or reentry if less than 7 days).

source.quote: Column 1: Check if the resident is taking any medications by pharmacological classification during the 7-day observation period (or since admission/entry or reentry if less than 7 days).

federal_coding_rules.rule: N0415B1: check if an anxiolytic medication was taken by the resident at any time during the 7-day look-back period (or since admission/entry or reentry if less than 7 days).

source.quote: N0415B1. Antianxiety: Check if an anxiolytic medication was taken by the resident at any time during the 7-day look-back period (or since admission/entry or reentry if less than 7 days).

federal_coding_rules.rule: N0415B2: check if there is an indication noted for ALL anxiolytic medications taken by the resident any time during the observation period (or since admission/entry or reentry if less than 7 days).

source.quote: N0415B2. Antianxiety: Check if there is an indication noted for all anxiolytic medications taken by the resident any time during the observation period (or since admission/entry or reentry if less than 7 days).

federal_coding_rules.rule: Code medications according to the medication's therapeutic category and/or pharmacological classification, not how it is used; e.g., oxazepam prescribed for use as a hypnotic is categorized as an antianxiety medication and is coded as antianxiety, not as a hypnotic.

source.quote: Code medications in Item N0415 according to the medication's therapeutic category and/or pharmacological classification, not how it is used. For example, although oxazepam may be prescribed for use as a hypnotic, it is categorized as an antianxiety medication.

federal_coding_rules.rule: Medications with more than one therapeutic category and/or pharmacological classification are coded in all categories/classifications assigned to the medication, regardless of how the medication is being used.

source.quote: Medications that have more than one therapeutic category and/or pharmacological classification should be coded in all categories/classifications assigned to the medication, regardless of how it is being used.

federal_coding_rules.rule: Include any of these medications given to the resident by any route in any setting (e.g., at the nursing home, in a hospital emergency room) while a resident of the nursing home.

source.quote: Include any of these medications given to the resident by any route in any setting (e.g., at the nursing home, in a hospital emergency room) while a resident of the nursing home.

federal_coding_rules.rule: Code a medication even if it was given only once during the look-back period.

source.quote: Code a medication even if it was given only once during the look-back period.

federal_coding_rules.rule: Count long-acting medications given every few weeks or monthly only if they are given during the 7-day look-back period (or since admission/entry or reentry if less than 7 days).

source.quote: Count long-acting medications, such as fluphenazine decanoate or haloperidol decanoate, that are given every few weeks or monthly only if they are given during the 7-day lookback period (or since admission/entry or reentry if less than 7 days).

federal_coding_rules.rule: For transdermal patches, only capture the medication if the transdermal patch was applied to the resident's skin during the observation period.

source.quote: To code N0415, only capture the medication if the transdermal patch was applied to the resident's skin during the observation period.

federal_coding_rules.rule: Combination medications should be coded in all categories/pharmacologic classes that constitute the combination.

source.quote: Combination medications should be coded in all categories/pharmacologic classes that constitute the combination.

federal_coding_rules.rule: Herbal and alternative medicine products (e.g., melatonin, chamomile, valerian root) are considered dietary supplements and should not be counted as medications.

source.quote: Therefore, they should not be counted as medications (e.g., melatonin, chamomile, valerian root).

federal_coding_rules.rule: Example application: lorazepam 1 mg PO QAM received every day for bipolar disorder is coded N0415B1 and N0415B2 checked — lorazepam is an antianxiety medication and the indication of use (bipolar disorder) is noted.

source.quote: N0415B1 and N0415B2. Antianxiety = checked; lorazepam is an antianxiety medication and indication of use for bipolar disorder noted.

federal_coding_rules.rule: N0415Z1, None of the above, is checked if none of the listed medications (including antianxiety) were taken by the resident at any time during the observation period (or since admission/entry or reentry if less than 7 days).

source.quote: N0415Z1. None of the above: Check if none of the medications above were taken by the resident at any time during the observation period (or since admission/entry or reentry if less than 7 days).

federal.criterion: Review the resident's medical record for documentation that any of these medications were received by the resident and for the indication of their use during the 7-day look-back period (or since admission/entry or reentry if less than 7 days).

source.quote: Review the resident's medical record for documentation that any of these medications were received by the resident and for the indication of their use during the 7-day lookback period (or since admission/entry or reentry if less than 7 days).

federal.notes: Step 1 of Steps for Assessment; establishes both the receipt of the medication and the indication as record-documented facts.

federal.criterion: Review documentation from other health care settings where the resident may have received any of these medications while a resident of the nursing home (e.g., valium given in the emergency room).

source.quote: Review documentation from other health care settings where the resident may have received any of these medications while a resident of the nursing home (e.g., valium given in the emergency room).

federal.notes: Step 2 of Steps for Assessment; the manual's own example is an antianxiety medication.

federal.criterion: An indication is the identified, DOCUMENTED clinical rationale for administering a medication, based upon a physician's (or prescriber's) assessment of the resident's condition and therapeutic goals.

source.quote: INDICATION The identified, documented clinical rationale for administering a medication that is based upon a physician's (or prescriber's) assessment of the resident's condition and therapeutic goals.

federal.notes: Definition governing whether Column 2 (N0415B2) may be checked.

federal.criterion: Assessors should be able to identify the source(s) used to support coding the MDS 3.0 pharmacological classification; facilities may wish to identify a consistently used resource.

source.quote: Facilities may wish to identify a resource that their staff consistently use to identify pharmacological classification as assessors should be able to identify the source(s) used to support coding the MDS 3.0.

federal.notes: Framed as a suggestion ("may wish") but with an expectation that the classification source be identifiable.

federal.criterion: Assessors should consult the manufacturer's package insert, which may contain the medication's pharmacological classification, and may work with the resident's pharmacist to confirm classification(s).

source.quote: Assessors should consult the manufacturer's package insert, which may contain the medication's pharmacological classification.

federal.criterion: When a resident receives antipsychotic, antianxiety and hypnotic medications simultaneously there must be a clear clinical indication for their use; adequate documentation is essential in justifying their use.

source.quote: Please note: if a resident is receiving medications in all three of these high-risk drug classes simultaneously there must be a clear clinical indication for the use of these medications.

federal.notes: Stated in the note following the N0415 example; the manual adds that administration in this combination could be interpreted as chemically restraining the resident.

federal.criterion: Providers are responsible for coding each medication's pharmacological/therapeutic classification accurately; the listed resources are informational only and their use is not required for MDS completion.

source.quote: Providers are responsible for coding each medication's pharmacological/therapeutic classification accurately.

case_mix_relevance.notes: The supplied Section N pages do not tie N0415B (Antianxiety) to any payment or case-mix classification.
